text:
Ethan Park: We need to nail down how we store + surface “previous known good version” (PKGV) in control plane so installer can do one-click rollback (and Support can see it in diagnostics). What’s the right source of truth + update semantics?

Benji Okafor: +1. Right now installer is tracking “last chart version installed” locally, but that’s not reliable (new operator laptop, air-gapped, etc). Control plane should own PKGV per deployment.

Connor O'Brien: Release Eng angle: it needs to be immutable-ish. Meaning: only updated after we know the upgrade actually succeeded (post-upgrade gates), not just “helm upgrade returned 0”. Otherwise rollback can point to a broken build.

Ines Carvalho: Agree. Also for Private we have multiple “versions”:
- control-plane app version
- runtime version(s)
- gateway version
- helm chart version(s)
- observability agent bundle
We probably need a PKGV *bundle* not a single string.

Michael Nguyen: From migrations side: PKGV can’t ignore schema state. If we persist “previous” but DB migrations are forward-only, rollback has to be blocked or treated as “best effort”. We added migration metadata to detect forward-only vs reversible. We should wire that into the PKGV object or at least into the rollback precheck.

Ethan Park: So proposal: control plane stores two things:
1) “current desired” (what target version the operator requested)
2) “last_known_good” (the last state that passed health+smoke gates)
Then installer calls an API like `GET /private/deployments/:id/version_state`.

Kenji Nakamura: UX question: “one-click rollback” in installer should show what it’s rolling back *to* (and why). Example: “Rollback to 1.12.3 (last healthy on Feb 24)”. If we don’t store timestamp + reason, we end up with scary prompts.

Sean Gallagher: SRE requirement: definition of “known good” must include some minimum steady-state window. I’d rather not mark it known-good until:
- control plane healthy
- gateway serving
- runtime passes smoke test
- no crash loops for N minutes
and ideally we record the upgrade correlation id for traceability.

Allison Grant: + observability: if control plane stores PKGV, we should emit an audit log + metric when it’s updated ("pkv_updated" or similar) so we can track unexpected churn.

Benji Okafor: Implementation thought: add a table `deployment_release_state` keyed by deployment_id.
Columns:
- deployment_id
- current_version_bundle (json)
- desired_version_bundle (json)
- previous_known_good_bundle (json)
- last_successful_upgrade_run_id
- last_successful_at
- last_failed_upgrade_run_id
- last_failed_at

Connor O'Brien: If we go JSON column, make sure it’s stable schema. We’ll regret it if installer relies on ad-hoc keys.

Ethan Park: We can define a versioned envelope:
```
VersionBundleV1:
  control_plane:
    app_version: "1.13.0"
    chart_version: "private-control-plane-0.42.0"
  gateway:
    chart_version: "private-gateway-0.18.2"
  runtime:
    image_digest: "sha256:..."
    runtime_version: "runtime-2.9.1"
  observability:
    bundle_version: "obs-pack-0.31.0"
  compatibility:
    matrix_id: "2026-02-15"
```
Installer only needs to treat it as opaque-ish but show major fields.

Michael Nguyen: Please don’t make “PKGV = chart versions only”. Rollback restoring chart versions while DB is at a newer schema is what causes bad states. We need rollback precheck to query migrations metadata:
- current_schema_version
- target_schema_version
- downgrade_supported (true/false)
If false, rollback should be blocked (or require an `--ack-forward-only-migrations` flag + tell operator it won’t restore DB).

Sean Gallagher: Strong preference: default block. Support will otherwise get dragged into “why did rollback make it worse”.

Kenji Nakamura: +1 to default block with a very clear message. If we allow override, it should be intentionally ugly (multiple prompts, requires `--force`).

Benji Okafor: Where do we compute “known good”? Installer is orchestrator today. If installer tells control plane “mark this as known good” after it runs post-upgrade smoke tests, that’s simplest.

Ethan Park: Yeah, installer is the one that knows when it completed the whole plan. Control plane can validate it’s in a healthy state but shouldn’t own orchestration (yet). API shape:
- `POST /private/deployments/:id/upgrade_runs` (create)
- `PATCH .../upgrade_runs/:run_id` (step updates)
- `POST .../upgrade_runs/:run_id/mark_success` (control plane checks health, writes PKGV)

Connor O'Brien: That works for online VPC. For air-gapped on-prem, installer still has to work with minimal dependencies. But it can still call control plane inside the cluster, so fine.

Allison Grant: When PKGV updates, make sure we include:
- run_id
- correlation_id
- operator identity (from installer auth / cert)
That’s needed for audit + troubleshooting.

Sean Gallagher: Also: partial upgrades. If upgrade fails mid-way and operator retries, PKGV should still be the last stable one, not “whatever we were halfway through”. So update PKGV only on mark_success, never on plan start.

Ines Carvalho: Edge case: first install / fresh cluster. PKGV is null. Rollback command should handle that gracefully ("no known good version recorded"). Also we should store “initial install version” as known good once the install passes the same smoke gates.

Michael Nguyen: Another edge: hotfix rollback. If you upgrade from 1.12.3 -> 1.12.4 and it passes, PKGV becomes 1.12.4. But if 1.12.4 later regresses due to workload, rollback to 1.12.3 might still be desired. That suggests we may want a small history (like last 2 successful) not just a single PKGV.

Connor O'Brien: I’d keep v1 minimal: one PKGV + last_failed. History is nice but can come later.

Ethan Park: Agree, but we can store it in upgrade_runs table and keep run records for e.g. 30 days. PKGV pointer can be “last_successful_run_id”. That gives history without separate schema.

Benji Okafor: Sounds good. Then `GET version_state` returns:
- current running bundle (as observed by CP)
- desired bundle (if any)
- previous known good bundle (from last_successful_run)
- downgrade_allowed boolean + message

Kenji Nakamura: Please include a single “recommended action” string in the response for installer UX. Example: "Rollback supported: run `redwood-private rollback --to known-good`" vs "Rollback blocked: forward-only DB migration detected".

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also ensure response is safe to include in diagnostics tarball (no secrets). Version strings + digests are fine.

Allison Grant: Naming: can we avoid "known good" vs "known-good" variations? Pick one term in API + docs. Observability will key off it.

Ethan Park: Action items:
- Ethan: draft API spec + table sketch (upgrade_runs + deployment_release_state pointer)
- Michael: confirm downgrade gating fields from migrations metadata and recommended error text
- Kenji: propose installer prompt copy for rollback-to-known-good
- Connor/Sean: define “mark_success” criteria (minimum healthy window + smoke tests)

Connor O'Brien: I’ll sync w/ Devon (installer) too — installer needs a stable contract. If CP returns PKGV bundle + downgrade_allowed, rollback can be a single flag.

Sean Gallagher: Please loop in Rafael for runbook updates once we settle this.

Ethan Park: Will do. I’ll post a doc link once drafted.
